speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing frequent nosebleeds and bleeding from your mucous membranes, along with small red spots on your skin. To help me understand what is causing this, when did you first notice these symptoms, and have you had any recent illnesses or fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any bleeding during urination or in the stool, and has the child experienced any recent bruising on the trunk or face? Also, are there any family history of bleeding disorders or recent exposure to new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have any enlarged lymph nodes, liver, or spleen, and has there been any recent unintentional weight loss or night sweats? I would also like to see if there are any palpable purpura or joint swelling present. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Physical examination notes: Diffuse petechiae noted on the patient's forearms, legs, and a few on his trunk. No significant ecchymosis or active bleeding sites noted. Mild bleeding noted from the gums on gentle probing. No active epistaxis at the time of the exam, but dried blood is noted at the nares. No information provided regarding enlarged lymph nodes, liver, spleen, unintentional weight loss, night sweats, palpable purpura, or joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, we must rule out a coagulation factor deficiency or a qualitative platelet defect. REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time, Bleeding_Time

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 12 seconds (normal); Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT): 30 seconds (normal); Bleeding Time: Information not available in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since PT and aPTT are normal, we need to evaluate for a qualitative platelet disorder or von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Function_Assay, Von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Function Assay (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Von Willebrand Factor Antigen: Information not available in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The platelet function assay shows a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors, which is the hallmark of Glanzmann thrombasthenia. Given the clinical presentation of mucocutaneous bleeding with normal platelet counts and coagulation studies, I am confident in this conclusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
